subject.title: Architecture: Consolidate ~15 custom boundary check scripts into unified tooling

question: Should OpenClaw consolidate boundary guards through a new config-driven checker, through incremental Oxlint/shared-helper migrations, or keep the current bespoke scripts?
rationale: The remaining work is an internal CI architecture direction that can trade enforcement precision, CI speed, and maintenance cost; automation should not pick that permanent rule shape without maintainer intent.

options.title: Incremental Wrapper/Oxlint Path
options.body: Migrate simple rules through existing wrappers and Oxlint configs, extract shared helpers for harder AST/file-walk guards, and require parity tests for each moved rule.

options.title: New Config Runner
options.body: Build a dedicated config-driven architecture-check runner and migrate representative guards only after maintainers accept the new framework as a long-term surface.

options.title: Keep Bespoke Guards
options.body: Close or defer the consolidation if the current independent scripts are preferred for precision and owner-local evolution despite the maintenance overhead.

recommendation.title: Incremental Wrapper/Oxlint Path
recommendation.body: Migrate simple rules through existing wrappers and Oxlint configs, extract shared helpers for harder AST/file-walk guards, and require parity tests for each moved rule.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main ownership is strongest on the boundary runner/package-script surface and related wrapper behavior.
